Batrachocephalus mino (Hamilton, 1822), the beardless sea catfish, is the only species of catfish (order Siluriformes) in the genus Batrachocephalus of the family Ariidae.

  • Common name: Beardless sea catfish
  • Synonyms: Ageneiosus mino, Batrachocephalus ageneiosus, Batrachocephalus micropogon
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
Indo-West Pacific: Bay of Bengal, and parts of the western central Pacific, in coastal waters, estuaries, and lower reaches of rivers. Type locality: Upper part of [Ganges] estuaries.
Found in marine coastal waters, as well as in estuaries and tidal rivers.

Etymology: The genus name Batrachocephalus: bátrachos, frog; cephalus, from kephal, head, referring to the frog-like head of B. ageneiosus (= mino). The species epithet mino: presumably a local name for this fish along upper Ganges estuaries in India.
